title: Extending Mandatory Timeframe for Consumption of Government-Paid Paternity Leave to 24 Months of Childbirth
what_it_is: Extending Mandatory Timeframe for Consumption of Government-Paid Paternity Leave to 24 Months of Childbirth

sections.label: Fathers' leave after childbirth
sections.summary: Fathers can take up to eight weeks of leave in the year after their child's birth, and there are no plans to extend paternity leave to 24 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Today, fathers can tap on up to eight weeks of leave in the year after their child's birth, including two weeks of paternity leave and four weeks of shared parental leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Similar to maternity leave, paternity leave should be consumed within 12 months of childbirth, as it is meant to support working fathers in caring for their infants when they are younger and in need of more care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For this reason, we have no plans to extend it to 24 months of childbirth.

sections.label: Leave support after child turns one
sections.summary: After a child turns one, parents can take unpaid infant care leave, paid childcare leave, and employers are encouraged to provide up to four weeks of unpaid leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: After the child turns one, parents can continue to tap on other forms of leave support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This includes six days of unpaid infant care leave per parent per year until the child turns two, on top of six days of paid childcare leave, which each parent can take annually until the child turns seven.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Together with the tripartite partners, we also encourage employers to provide up to four weeks of unpaid leave per year if their employees have children below two years old who need more care, for example, due to medical conditions.

sections.label: Fathers not taking paternity leave
sections.summary: In 2018, 65% of fathers in Singapore did not take even one day of paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What was shocking for me was that in 2018, 65% of fathers in Singapore did not even take one day of paternity leave.

sections.label: Paternity leave utilisation rate
sections.summary: Paternity leave utilisation is around 3%, which is very low.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Paternity leave utilisation is around 3%, very low.

sections.label: Current paternity leave utilisation
sections.summary: Today, the paternity leave utilisation is about 53%, which is not too bad.
